sanskrit: tatropaviṣṭau muditau nākapṛṣṭhe 'śvināv iva abhyagacchat tadā vipro vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: While the two sat there in joy, like the Aśvins in heaven, a brahmin then approached Vāsudeva and Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: bṛhacchālapratīkāśaḥ prataptakanakaprabhaḥ haripiṅgo hariśmaśruḥ pramāṇāyāmataḥ samaḥ
english: He was like a great sala tree in stature, shining like refined gold, tawny-complexioned with a tawny beard, perfectly proportioned in height and breadth.

sanskrit: taruṇādityasaṃkāśaḥ kṛṣṇavāsā jaṭādharaḥ padmapatrānanaḥ piṅgas tejasā prajvalann iva
english: He resembled the rising sun, clad in dark garments, wearing matted locks, with a face like a lotus petal, tawny-hued, blazing as if with inner fire.

sanskrit: upasṛṭaṃ tu taṃ kṛṣṇau bhrājamānaṃ dvijottamam arjuno vāsudevaś ca tūrṇam utpatya tasthatuḥ
english: When that radiant best-of-twice-born approached, Arjuna and Vāsudeva quickly rose and stood to receive him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca so 'bravīd arjunaṃ caiva vāsudevaṃ ca sātvatam lokapravīrau tiṣṭhantau khāṇḍavasya samīpataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: He spoke to Arjuna and to Vāsudeva of the Sātvata clan, those two heroes of the world standing near the Khandava forest.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo bahubhoktāsmi bhuñje 'parimitaṃ sadā bhikṣe vārṣṇeyapārthau vām ekāṃ tṛptiṃ prayacchatām
english: "I am a brahmin who eats much; I always eat without limit. I beg of you, O Vārṣṇeya and Pārtha — grant me one single satisfaction."

sanskrit: evam uktau tam abrūtāṃ tatas tau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau kenānnena bhavāṃs tṛpyet tasyānnasya yatāvahe
english: Thus addressed, Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava said to him: "With what food shall you be satisfied? We shall procure that food for you."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa bhagavān abravīt tāv ubhau tataḥ bhāṣamāṇau tadā vīrau kim annaṃ kriyatām iti
english: Thus questioned, the blessed one then spoke to both those heroes who had asked what food should be obtained:

sanskrit: nāham annaṃ bubhukṣe vai pāvakaṃ māṃ nibodhatam yadannam anurūpaṃ me tad yuvāṃ saṃprayacchatam
english: "I do not hunger for ordinary food — know me as Fire! The food that befits me — that you two shall give me."

sanskrit: idam indraḥ sadā dāvaṃ khāṇḍavaṃ parirakṣati taṃ na śaknomy ahaṃ dagdhuṃ rakṣyamāṇaṃ mahātmanā
english: "Indra constantly protects this forest of Khandava. I cannot burn it while it is protected by that great-souled one."

sanskrit: vasaty atra sakhā tasya takṣakaḥ pannagaḥ sadā sagaṇas tatkṛte dāvaṃ parirakṣati vajrabhṛt
english: "His friend the serpent Takṣaka dwells here always, and on his account Indra the wielder of the vajra guards this forest together with his retinue."

sanskrit: tatra bhūtāny anekāni rakṣyante sma prasaṅgataḥ taṃ didhakṣur na śaknomi dagdhuṃ śakrasya tejasā
english: "Many beings are protected there along with him. Wishing to burn it, I am unable to do so because of Śakra's power."

sanskrit: sa māṃ prajvalitaṃ dṛṣṭvā meghāmbhobhiḥ pravarṣati tato dagdhuṃ na śaknomi didhakṣur dāvam īpsitam
english: "Seeing me ablaze, he pours down torrents of cloud-water, and thus I cannot burn the desired forest, though I wish to consume it."

sanskrit: sa yuvābhyāṃ sahāyābhyām astravidbhyāṃ samāgataḥ daheyaṃ khāṇḍavaṃ dāvam etad annaṃ vṛtaṃ mayā
english: "With you two as helpers — masters of weapons — I can burn the Khandava forest. This is the food I have chosen."

sanskrit: yuvāṃ hy udakadhārās tā bhūtāni ca samantataḥ uttamāstravido samyak sarvato vārayiṣyathaḥ
english: "For you two, skilled in the best weapons, shall properly ward off those streams of water and block the creatures from escaping in every direction."

sanskrit: evam ukte pratyuvāca bībhatsur jātavedasam didhakṣuṃ khāṇḍavaṃ dāvam akāmasya śatakratoḥ
english: When thus addressed, Bībhatsu (Arjuna) replied to Jātaveda (Fire), who desired to burn the Khandava forest against the will of Śatakratu (Indra):

sanskrit: uttamāstrāṇi me santi divyāni ca bahūni ca yair ahaṃ śaknuyāṃ yoddhum api vajradharān bahūn
english: "I possess many excellent weapons, both divine and otherwise, with which I could fight even many wielders of the thunderbolt."

sanskrit: dhanur me nāsti bhagavan bāhuvīryeṇa saṃmitam kurvataḥ samare yatnaṃ vegaṃ yad viṣaheta me
english: "But I have no bow, O blessed one, equal to the strength of my arms — one that could endure my speed and exertion in battle."

sanskrit: śaraiś ca me 'rtho bahubhir akṣayaiḥ kṣipram asyataḥ na hi voḍhuṃ rathaḥ śaktaḥ śarān mama yathepsitān
english: "I also need many inexhaustible arrows, for I shoot swiftly; no chariot is capable of carrying as many arrows as I desire."

sanskrit: aśvāṃś ca divyān iccheyaṃ pāṇḍurān vātaraṃhasaḥ rathaṃ ca meghanirghoṣaṃ sūryapratimatejasam
english: "I would also want divine white horses swift as the wind, and a chariot that thunders like a cloud and blazes like the sun."

sanskrit: tathā kṛṣṇasya vīryeṇa nāyudhaṃ vidyate samam yena nāgān piśācāṃś ca nihanyān mādhavo raṇe
english: "Likewise, there is no weapon equal to the valor of Kṛṣṇa — one with which Mādhava could slay nagas and pisachas in battle."

sanskrit: upāyaṃ karmaṇaḥ siddhau bhagavan vaktum arhasi nivārayeyaṃ yenendraṃ varṣamāṇaṃ mahāvane
english: "O blessed one, you should indicate the means for the task's success — the means by which I could ward off Indra as he pours rain over the great forest."

sanskrit: pauruṣeṇa tu yat kāryaṃ tat kartārau sva pāvaka karaṇāni samarthāni bhagavan dātum arhasi
english: "What is to be done through manly valor — that we two shall do, O Fire! But the capable instruments, O blessed one, you should provide."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu bhagavān dhūmaketur hutāśanaḥ cintayām āsa varuṇaṃ lokapālaṃ didṛkṣayā ādityam udake devaṃ nivasantaṃ jaleśvaram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the blessed one — Smoke-bannered Fire, the Oblation-eater — thought of Varuṇa, the guardian of the world, the sun-born god dwelling in the waters, the lord of the ocean, wishing to see him.

sanskrit: sa ca tac cintitaṃ jñātvā darśayām āsa pāvakam tam abravīd dhūmaketuḥ pratipūjya jaleśvaram caturthaṃ lokapālānāṃ rakṣitāraṃ maheśvaram
english: Knowing that thought, Varuṇa appeared before Fire. Smoke-bannered Fire, having duly honored the lord of the waters — the great lord, the fourth among the world-guardians — then spoke to him:

sanskrit: somena rājñā yad dattaṃ dhanuś caiveṣudhī ca te tat prayacchobhayaṃ śīghraṃ rathaṃ ca kapilakṣaṇam
english: "That bow and those two quivers given to you by King Soma — hand them both over quickly, along with the chariot marked with a tawny emblem."

sanskrit: kāryaṃ hi sumahat pārtho gāṇḍīvena kariṣyati cakreṇa vāsudevaś ca tan madarthe pradīyatām dadānīty eva varuṇaḥ pāvakaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: "For Pārtha shall accomplish a very great task with the Gāṇḍīva, and Vāsudeva with the discus. Let them be given for my sake." And Varuṇa replied to Fire: "I shall give them."

sanskrit: tato 'dbhutaṃ mahāvīryaṃ yaśaḥkīrtivivardhanam sarvaśastrair anādhṛṣyaṃ sarvaśastrapramāthi ca sarvāyudhamahāmātraṃ parasenāpradharṣaṇam
english: Then he brought forth that wondrous bow of great power, enhancer of fame and glory, invincible against all weapons, destroyer of all weapons, the great measure of all arms, the crusher of enemy armies —

sanskrit: ekaṃ śatasahasreṇa saṃmitaṃ rāṣṭravardhanam citram uccāvacair varṇaiḥ śobhitaṃ ślakṣṇam avraṇam
english: — worth a hundred thousand ordinary bows, increaser of kingdoms, beautiful with many-colored markings, smooth and without blemish —

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvaiḥ pūjitaṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ prādād vai dhanuratnaṃ tad akṣayyau ca maheṣudhī
english: — honored by gods, danavas, and gandharvas through endless ages. He gave that jewel of a bow, the Gāṇḍīva, and also two inexhaustible great quivers.

sanskrit: rathaṃ ca divyāśvayujaṃ kapipravaraketanam upetaṃ rājatair aśvair gāndharvair hemamālibhiḥ pāṇḍurābhrapratīkāśair manovāyusamair jave
english: And also a chariot yoked to divine horses, bearing the banner of the chief of monkeys, fitted with silver horses of the Gandharva breed, garlanded with gold, white as autumn clouds, equal to mind and wind in speed —

sanskrit: sarvopakaraṇair yuktam ajayyaṃ devadānavaiḥ bhānumantaṃ mahāghoṣaṃ sarvabhūtamanoharam
english: — equipped with every fitting accessory, unconquerable by gods and danavas, blazing with light, of great thunder, pleasing to all beings.

sanskrit: sasarja yat svatapasā bhauvano bhuvanaprabhuḥ prajāpatir anirdeśyaṃ yasya rūpaṃ raver iva
english: That chariot had been fashioned by Prajāpati the lord of the world, the earthly creator, through his own austerities — its form as indescribable as the sun's.

sanskrit: yaṃ sma somaḥ samāruhya dānavān ajayat prabhuḥ nagameghapratīkāśaṃ jvalantam iva ca śriyā
english: Mounting that chariot, the powerful Soma had once conquered the danavas — it resembled a mountain or cloud and blazed with glory.

sanskrit: āśritā taṃ rathaśreṣṭhaṃ śakrāyudhasamā śubhā tāpanīyā surucirā dhvajayaṣṭir anuttamā
english: Adorning that finest of chariots was a flagstaff of gold equal to Indra's weapon, auspicious, very beautiful, unsurpassed.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ tu vānaro divyaḥ siṃhaśārdūlalakṣaṇaḥ vinardann iva tatrasthaḥ saṃsthito mūrdhny aśobhata
english: Upon it a divine monkey, bearing the marks of a lion and tiger, stationed as if roaring, blazed gloriously at the summit.

sanskrit: dhvaje bhūtāni tatrāsan vividhāni mahānti ca nādena ripusainyānāṃ yeṣāṃ saṃjñā praṇaśyati
english: On the banner too were various great beings whose roar causes the consciousness of enemy armies to vanish.

sanskrit: sa taṃ nānāpatākābhiḥ śobhitaṃ ratham uttamam pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtya daivatebhyaḥ praṇamya ca
english: Arjuna circumambulated that finest chariot adorned with many banners, going around it clockwise, and bowed to the gods.

sanskrit: saṃnaddhaḥ kavacī khaḍgī baddhagodhāṅgulitravān āruroha rathaṃ pārtho vimānaṃ sukṛtī yathā
english: Armored, bearing sword, with his leather wrist-guard bound on, Pārtha mounted the chariot as a man of good deeds mounts a celestial car.

sanskrit: tac ca divyaṃ dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ purā gāṇḍīvam upasaṃgṛhya babhūva mudito 'rjunaḥ
english: And taking up that divine best-of-bows, the Gāṇḍīva fashioned long ago by Brahmā, Arjuna was filled with joy.

sanskrit: hutāśanaṃ namaskṛtya tatas tad api vīryavān jagrāha balam āsthāya jyayā ca yuyuje dhanuḥ
english: After bowing to Fire, the valiant one then took it up with full strength and strung the bow with its bowstring.

sanskrit: maurvyāṃ tu yujyamānāyāṃ balinā pāṇḍavena ha ye 'śṛṇvan kūjitaṃ tatra teṣāṃ vai vyathitaṃ manaḥ
english: When that bowstring was drawn by the mighty Pāṇḍava, those who heard the twang were afflicted in their hearts.

sanskrit: labdhvā rathaṃ dhanuś caiva tathākṣayyau maheṣudhī babhūva kalyaḥ kaunteyaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sāhyakarmaṇi
english: Having obtained the chariot, the bow, and the two inexhaustible great quivers, the son of Kuntī was ready and delighted to render assistance.

sanskrit: vajranābhaṃ tataś cakraṃ dadau kṛṣṇāya pāvakaḥ āgneyam astraṃ dayitaṃ sa ca kalyo 'bhavat tadā
english: Then Fire gave to Kṛṣṇa the discus with the thunderbolt-navel — the beloved fiery weapon — and Kṛṣṇa too became ready.

sanskrit: abravīt pāvakaś cainam etena madhusūdana amānuṣān api raṇe vijeṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ
english: And Fire said to him: "With this, O Madhusūdana, you shall conquer even superhuman foes in battle — there is no doubt."

sanskrit: anena tvaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ devānām api cāhave rakṣaḥpiśācadaityānāṃ nāgānāṃ cādhikaḥ sadā bhaviṣyasi na saṃdehaḥ pravarārinibarhaṇe
english: "With this you shall always be superior to humans and even gods in battle, to rakshasas, pisachas, daityas, and nagas — no doubt, O slayer of foremost enemies."

sanskrit: kṣiptaṃ kṣiptaṃ raṇe caitat tvayā mādhava śatruṣu hatvāpratihataṃ saṃkhye pāṇim eṣyati te punaḥ
english: "Hurled again and again in battle by you, O Mādhava, against your enemies, it shall kill without obstruction and return to your hand in combat."

sanskrit: varuṇaś ca dadau tasmai gadām aśaniniḥsvanām daityāntakaraṇīṃ ghorāṃ nāmnā kaumodakīṃ hareḥ
english: And Varuṇa gave him a mace that thundered like lightning, terrible, destroyer of daityas — Hari's (Viṣṇu's) mace named Kaumodaki.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāvakam abrūtāṃ prahṛṣṭau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau kṛtāstrau śastrasaṃpannau rathinau dhvajināv api
english: Then Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava, delighted, equipped with weapons and fully armed, mounted on chariots with their banners, spoke to Fire:

sanskrit: kalyau svo bhagavan yoddhum api sarvaiḥ surāsuraiḥ kiṃ punar vajriṇaikena pannagārthe yuyutsunā
english: "We are ready, O blessed one, to fight even all the gods and asuras together — how much more then against Indra alone who fights on behalf of the serpent!"

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca cakram astraṃ ca vārṣṇeyo visṛjan yudhi vīryavān triṣu lokeṣu tan nāsti yan na jīyāj janārdanaḥ
english: Arjuna said: "There is nothing in the three worlds that Janārdana the valiant Vārṣṇeya cannot conquer when releasing his discus and weapon in battle."

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvaṃ dhanur ādāya tathākṣayyau maheṣudhī aham apy utsahe lokān vijetuṃ yudhi pāvaka
english: "Taking up the Gāṇḍīva bow and the two inexhaustible great quivers, I too am bold enough to conquer the worlds in battle, O Fire."

sanskrit: sarvataḥ parivāryainaṃ dāvena mahatā prabho kāmaṃ saṃprajvalādyaiva kalyau svaḥ sāhyakarmaṇi
english: "Surround it on all sides with great blazing fire, O lord — blaze up this very day as you wish! We are ready to render assistance."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ sa bhagavān dāśārheṇārjunena ca taijasaṃ rūpam āsthāya dāvaṃ dagdhuṃ pracakrame
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the descendant of Dāśārha and by Arjuna, the blessed one assumed his fiery form and began to burn the forest.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ parivāryātha saptārcir jvalanas tadā dadāha khāṇḍavaṃ kruddho yugāntam iva darśayan
english: Surrounding it on all sides, the seven-tongued blazing fire then burned the Khandava in rage, presenting a sight like the end of an age.

sanskrit: parigṛhya samāviṣṭas tad vanaṃ bharatarṣabha meghastanitanirghoṣaṃ sarvabhūtāni nirdahan
english: Seizing and pervading that forest, O bull of the Bharatas, roaring like thunder from clouds, he consumed all living beings.

sanskrit: dahyatas tasya vibabhau rūpaṃ dāvasya bhārata meror iva nagendrasya kāñcanasya mahādyuteḥ
english: As it burned, O Bharata, the appearance of that forest blazed like the great-resplendent golden mountain Meru, king of peaks.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tau rathābhyāṃ naravyāghrau dāvasyobhayataḥ sthitau dikṣu sarvāsu bhūtānāṃ cakrāte kadanaṃ mahat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those two tigers among men, stationed on their chariots on both sides of the forest, caused great slaughter of the creatures in all directions.

sanskrit: yatra yatra hi dṛśyante prāṇinaḥ khāṇḍavālayāḥ palāyantas tatra tatra tau vīrau paryadhāvatām
english: Wherever creatures dwelling in the Khandava were seen fleeing, there those two heroes would rush to intercept them.

sanskrit: chidraṃ hi na prapaśyanti rathayor āśuvikramāt āviddhāv iva dṛśyete rathinau tau rathottamau
english: No gap was seen in their chariots because of their swift movement; those two supreme charioteers appeared as if whirling everywhere at once.

sanskrit: khāṇḍave dahyamāne tu bhūtāny atha sahasraśaḥ utpetur bhairavān nādān vinadanto diśo daśa
english: As the Khandava burned, thousands upon thousands of beings leaped up, uttering fearful cries in all ten directions.

sanskrit: dagdhaikadeśā bahavo niṣṭaptāś ca tathāpare sphuṭitākṣā viśīrṇāś ca viplutāś ca vicetasaḥ
english: Many had one part of their body burned; others were scorched all over; their eyes burst open; they fell apart and flew about, bereft of consciousness.

sanskrit: samāliṅgya sutān anye pitṝn mātṝṃs tathāpare tyaktuṃ na śekuḥ snehena tathaiva nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: Some embraced their sons, others their fathers and mothers; unable to abandon them out of love, they perished together with them.

sanskrit: vikṛtair darśanair anye samutpetuḥ sahasraśaḥ tatra tatra vighūrṇantaḥ punar agnau prapedire
english: Others by the thousands leaped up with distorted appearances, reeling to and fro, and fell back into the fire again.

sanskrit: dagdhapakṣākṣicaraṇā viceṣṭanto mahītale tatra tatra sma dṛśyante vinaśyantaḥ śarīriṇaḥ
english: Creatures with wings, eyes, and feet burned, writhing on the ground, were seen here and there perishing.

sanskrit: jalasthāneṣu sarveṣu kvāthyamāneṣu bhārata gatasattvāḥ sma dṛśyante kūrmamatsyāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: In all the water pools as they were boiled away, O Bharata, thousands of tortoises and fishes could be seen, their lives gone.

sanskrit: śarīraiḥ saṃpradīptaiś ca dehavanta ivāgnayaḥ adṛśyanta vane tasmin prāṇinaḥ prāṇasaṃkṣaye
english: With their bodies blazing, the creatures in that forest appeared like fires with bodies, as their life-breath was extinguished.

sanskrit: tāṃs tathotpatataḥ pārthaḥ śaraiḥ saṃchidya khaṇḍaśaḥ dīpyamāne tataḥ prāsyat prahasan kṛṣṇavartmani
english: Those that flew up, Pārtha cut into pieces with his arrows and cast them laughing into the blazing path of Fire.

sanskrit: te śarācitasarvāṅgā vinadanto mahāravān ūrdhvam utpatya vegena nipetuḥ pāvake punaḥ
english: Pierced in every limb by arrows, uttering great cries, they leaped upward with speed and fell back into the fire.

sanskrit: śarair abhyāhatānāṃ ca dahyatāṃ ca vanaukasām virāvaḥ śrūyate ha sma samudrasyeva mathyataḥ
english: The shriek of those forest-dwellers being struck by arrows and being burned was heard like the churning of the ocean.

sanskrit: vahneś cāpi prahṛṣṭasya kham utpetur mahārciṣaḥ janayām āsur udvegaṃ sumahāntaṃ divaukasām
english: From Fire blazing with joy, great flames shot into the sky, causing immense alarm among the denizens of heaven.

sanskrit: tato jagmur mahātmānaḥ sarva eva divaukasaḥ śaraṇaṃ devarājānaṃ sahasrākṣaṃ puraṃdaram
english: Then all the great-souled celestials went for refuge to the king of the gods, thousand-eyed Purandara (Indra).

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ kiṃ nv ime mānavāḥ sarve dahyante kṛṣṇavartmanā kaccin na saṃkṣayaḥ prāpto lokānām amareśvara
english: The gods said: "Why are all these beings burned by the path of Fire? Has the destruction of the worlds come, O lord of immortals?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā vṛtrahā tebhyaḥ svayam evānvavekṣya ca khāṇḍavasya vimokṣārthaṃ prayayau harivāhanaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Vṛtra-slayer (Indra) personally surveyed the situation and then set out to liberate the Khandava, riding his horse Hari.

sanskrit: mahatā meghajālena nānārūpeṇa vajrabhṛt ākāśaṃ samavastīrya pravavarṣa sureśvaraḥ
english: Covering the sky with a vast network of clouds of many forms, the wielder of the thunderbolt, lord of the gods, poured down rain.

sanskrit: tato 'kṣamātrā visṛjan dhārāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ abhyavarṣat sahasrākṣaḥ pāvakaṃ khāṇḍavaṃ prati
english: Then thousand-eyed Indra, releasing streams as large as axles, hundreds of thousands of them, rained upon Fire and the Khandava.

sanskrit: asaṃprāptās tu tā dhārās tejasā jātavedasaḥ kha eva samaśuṣyanta na kāś cit pāvakaṃ gatāḥ
english: But those streams, by the power of Jātaveda (Fire), dried up in mid-air before reaching him, not one of them reaching the fire.

sanskrit: tato namucihā kruddho bhṛśam arciṣmatas tadā punar evābhyavarṣat tam ambhaḥ pravisṛjan bahu
english: Then Namuci-slayer (Indra), enraged, released abundant water and rained down again upon the intensely blazing fire.

sanskrit: arcir dhārābhisaṃbaddhaṃ dhūmavidyutsamākulam babhūva tad vanaṃ ghoraṃ stanayitnusaghoṣavat
english: The forest became terrible, with flames intertwined with streams, filled with smoke and lightning, resounding like thunder.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasyābhivarṣato vāri pāṇḍavaḥ pratyavārayat śaravarṣeṇa bībhatsur uttamāstrāṇi darśayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As Indra poured down water, the Pāṇḍava Bībhatsu (Arjuna) counter-warded it with a shower of arrows, displaying his supreme weapons.
